intro.text: Here's what working with me looks like — no jargon to learn, no developer to wait on.

body.text: Say it like you'd say it to a person — in Claude on your computer: "Draft the reply to this email in our voice," or "Turn this spreadsheet into a monthly report."
Claude works in your own files and tools, under the house rules we wrote together — the draft is in your inbox, the report is in the folder. No ticket, no waiting.
You review before anything leaves the building, and I show you how to see and undo what it did. Guardrails are written down, not assumed.

note.text: Everything I set up runs on your computer under your accounts — if you and I part ways, you keep all of it. A website you change by texting is a different thing: that's [Patchlamp](#patchlamp), a service that runs on my systems, with its own plans and terms.

body.text: There are a lot of AI consultants right now. Most of them can't read the code the AI writes. I'm a full-stack engineer who builds and ships production software — which means when AI does the work, I can verify it, correct it, and put guardrails around it. That's the difference between "AI advice" and AI you can run your business on. [See my engineering work →](/)

question.text: Do I need to be technical?

answer.text: No. If you can describe what you want in a text message, you can use everything I set up. The technical part is my job — that's what the install is.

question.text: What if the AI breaks something?

answer.text: On your computer, Claude works inside the folders and rules we set, and I show you how to review and undo what it does in the first session. For a website changed by text, that's Patchlamp's job: every change is saved in the site's history and any change can be undone by asking.

Yes. Your accounts, your code, your data, and your AI subscription. Unlike all-in-one AI startups, nothing I set up holds your business hostage: the install runs on your machine under your account, and the written house rules are yours to keep.

The care plan is optional. AI tools change monthly, and a setup that isn't maintained slowly stops being useful; $79 a month keeps your install current, with a monthly check-in and a written report. Skip it and everything still works — you just maintain it yourself.
